definition: A geographical intelligence platform translating population density, place-based statistics and spatial relationships into immediate, comparable forms.
context: Metroplist began from a need to make complex place data understandable without stripping away its source, time period or geographic meaning.
The public website is one surface of a wider data-and-interpretation system intended to support comparison, exploration and later spatial experiences.
challenge: Population, transport, infrastructure and risk datasets arrive with different boundaries, definitions, release dates and levels of trust.
A conventional collection of charts would not provide a durable model for comparing places or explaining why two apparently similar figures may not describe the same thing.
proposition: Treat every displayed value as a traceable observation with source, geography, time and transformation history.
Translate density and place statistics into a consistent comparison language while preserving the ability to inspect the original record.
Build the website, future tools and exploratory interfaces as consumers of the same canonical spatial model.

role.summary: Product definition, data-system architecture, spatial reasoning, interface engineering, provenance design and technical direction.
responsibilities: Future AR and VR experience planning

architecture.title: Source and provenance layer
architecture.description: Records where each dataset came from, which geography and period it describes, and how it may be used or compared.

architecture.title: Canonical place model
architecture.description: Connects locations, boundaries, transport, density and other observations without flattening their different meanings into one number.

architecture.title: Translation layer
architecture.description: Converts statistical and spatial records into comparable forms, explanatory language and visual encodings.

architecture.title: Experience surfaces
architecture.description: Supports the public web interface now and leaves a coherent route into map, immersive, AR and VR experiences later.

decisions.title: Provenance before spectacle
decisions.description: The platform must be able to explain a value before using it in a compelling visual comparison.

decisions.title: Time-aware data
decisions.description: Place records must retain their observation period so historical and current states are not silently merged.

decisions.title: Multiple experiences, one model
decisions.description: Web, mapping and immersive outputs should consume the same resolved data rather than becoming independent products with conflicting facts.

constraints.title: Uneven public data
constraints.description: Coverage, update cadence and geographic precision vary between authorities and countries.

constraints.title: Current versus intended capability
constraints.description: The case study must distinguish implemented web and data foundations from planned global, AR and VR experiences.

currentState.summary: The active build establishes the project identity, public product experience and the foundations for a provenance-led data platform.

plannedDevelopment.summary: Development continues toward broader spatial coverage and richer ways to interrogate place relationships.

significance: Metroplist demonstrates that the engineering challenge is not drawing maps; it is building a trustworthy translation system between raw spatial evidence and human understanding.

evidence.note: Development imagery is presented separately from claims about implemented data coverage.

definition: A professional-audio product and service ecosystem connecting software instruments, effects, sound libraries, creator services, licensing and delivery infrastructure.
context: AudioRii grows from a long-standing ambition to develop original professional-audio equipment and software rather than only work within other manufacturers' systems.
The project is being built as an ecosystem: products, libraries and services share a signal-led language and a common operational foundation.
challenge: A credible audio-product company requires more than a website or a collection of plug-in mock-ups. Product identity, DSP and application direction, licensing, release pipelines, creator services and delivery infrastructure must develop as one system.
The architecture must support learning and prototyping now without closing off commercial software, hardware and cloud-assisted products later.
proposition: Define products, libraries and services as connected parts of one AudioRii platform.
Use a continuous signal-path grammar across identity, interfaces, diagrams and future physical controls.
Separate public product presentation from private engine, licensing, build and delivery infrastructure.

role.summary: System architecture, professional-audio product direction, software and web engineering, infrastructure planning, identity-system design and creator-platform definition.
responsibilities: Digital audio asset and creator workflow design

architecture.title: Products
architecture.description: RiiSign, RiiSampl and RiiPulsiv establish the initial software-product family, with room for further instruments, effects and hardware.

architecture.title: Libraries
architecture.description: Harmonic Atlas, Impulse Archive and Spatial Profiles organise reusable sound and acoustic intelligence.

architecture.title: Services
architecture.description: Soundbase, Creator Hub and related services provide learning, account, delivery and creator-facing capabilities.

architecture.title: Operational foundation
architecture.description: Private infrastructure supports builds, licensing, updates, deployment, automation and future cloud-assisted audio services.

decisions.title: Signal never teleports
decisions.description: Every visual and technical representation should imply a route, transformation boundary and continuation of signal.

decisions.title: Products first, platform underneath
decisions.description: The public experience presents understandable audio products while the shared engine and services remain modular beneath them.

decisions.title: Commercial boundaries remain explicit
decisions.description: Learning prototypes, open-source experiments and future closed-source releases must not be blurred into one licensing claim.

constraints.title: Early product stage
constraints.description: Product concepts and infrastructure are active development; mock-ups must not be described as released plug-ins.

constraints.title: Private engine work
constraints.description: Internal architecture and licensing detail should be evidenced without exposing sensitive implementation.

currentState.summary: AudioRii currently has a defined ecosystem, public website, product language, visual system, prototype product assets and operational infrastructure direction.
capabilities: Audio product and creator asset development

plannedDevelopment.summary: The next phases turn the product definitions into testable audio software and connect them to the private delivery platform.

significance: AudioRii brings Mike Gold's audio, software, infrastructure, product and identity disciplines into one deliberately engineered product company.

heroImage.caption: AudioRii public product and identity system

definition: A personalised annual-guide platform that resolves authoritative celestial state, natal and user context, interpretive rules and curated content into a canonical, versioned 365-day physical and digital Guide.
context: Visionary Guide is organised around a person ordering an individualised annual physical Guide, not around a generic horoscope feed.
The app, web experience, APIs and later exploratory products are consumers of the same generation and publication engine.
challenge: Astronomical state, natal context, interpretive rules, preferences and editorial content must resolve into one internally consistent annual dataset.
The generated Guide must be reproducible, auditable and frozen before publication so digital and physical outputs do not drift apart.
proposition: Calculate and validate authoritative celestial state independently from the interpretive layer.
Generate a canonical Guide dataset containing the complete annual sequence, version information and source snapshot.
Publish print, app and web outputs from the frozen dataset rather than recalculating content independently in each surface.

role.summary: Product architecture, generation-system design, astronomy and interpretation boundaries, data modelling, publication architecture, application direction and technical governance.
responsibilities: Web, app and API experience direction

architecture.title: Authoritative astronomy state
architecture.description: Resolves current, historical or future celestial positions from trusted ephemeris data without using the visual universe as a calculation source.

architecture.title: Interpretation engine
architecture.description: Applies natal context, aspects, houses, day types, preferences and proprietary interpretive rules as a separate, versioned layer.

architecture.title: Canonical Guide generation
architecture.description: Creates and freezes the person's complete annual Guide dataset with engine versions, source snapshots and audit information.

architecture.title: Publication system
architecture.description: Renders the canonical dataset into the physical 365-day Guide, app, web, downloads and future licensed outputs.

decisions.title: The physical annual Guide comes first
decisions.description: The generation algorithm and publication object organise the platform; the standalone app follows rather than replacing them.

decisions.title: Generation outputs are immutable
decisions.description: A published Guide remains tied to the exact data snapshot and engine versions used to produce it.

decisions.title: Mirror interactions do not rewrite print
decisions.description: Later reflective or exploratory products may learn from use, but they never silently alter an already generated physical Guide.

constraints.title: Controlled disclosure
constraints.description: The public case study should demonstrate responsive application and publication engineering without revealing proprietary rules or premature product detail.

constraints.title: Current versus future consumers
constraints.description: The annual Guide and core generation system must remain clearly distinct from later Mirror, AR, marketplace and licensing extensions.

currentState.summary: The active project has a defined canonical architecture, product sequence, publication model and public application direction.
capabilities: Annual Guide product and data model
Responsive app and web experience development

plannedDevelopment.summary: Development proceeds from authoritative calculation and canonical generation into publication, account and companion-app implementation.

significance: Visionary Guide demonstrates the design of a publication product whose trust depends on data lineage, interpretive governance and reproducible generation—not merely interface styling.

evidence.note: Only deliberately public interface evidence is shown. Compact and developmental component studies remain supporting material rather than the main reveal.

definition: An adaptive learning institution, online school and teaching platform organised around different learners, subjects and pathways through knowledge.
context: Bjórr combines an enduring institutional structure with learner-controlled environments and adaptive pathways.
The School and the wider Institution share a family identity while retaining distinct public, learning and governance roles.
challenge: The platform must remain coherent across public prospectus, authenticated learning, learner progress and institutional record.
Adaptation should support the learner without turning the system into an opaque or unbounded authority.
proposition: Separate School, learner and Institution environments while preserving a shared knowledge model.
Keep learner state, pathway, course and mastery relationships visible and understandable.
Allow controlled visual adaptation without changing the information hierarchy or learning structure.

role.summary: Institution and product architecture, learning-system design, adaptive interface engineering, account and pathway modelling, identity architecture and technical direction.

architecture.title: Public School
architecture.description: Presents the learning proposition, subjects and routes into study.

architecture.title: Learner environment
architecture.description: Connects active fields, pathways, courses, activities, progress and bounded adaptive observations.

architecture.title: Bjórr Institution
architecture.description: Provides the wider research, governance and public-record register.

architecture.title: Connected identity system
architecture.description: Uses distinct School and Institution registers without fragmenting recognition.

currentState.summary: Bjórr has a substantial public, learner and institutional interface system alongside a developed identity architecture and adaptive learning model.

plannedDevelopment.summary: Further work will deepen learning content, adaptation rules, institutional governance and the connection between study evidence and progression.

significance: Bjórr is a strong example of product, education, identity and interface architecture operating as one institution rather than as separate website features.

definition: A modular retail and distribution platform built to support products, brand records, exclusive ranges and future fulfilment relationships.
context: Community Supplies is being established as an independent commerce system rather than a generic storefront skin.
Its catalogue must accommodate products, brands, ranges and future operational relationships without tying the public experience to one inherited content model.
challenge: Retail presentation, catalogue structure and distribution requirements often become entangled inside page templates.
The platform needs a durable product and brand model that can support new ranges and fulfilment arrangements without repeatedly rebuilding the storefront.
proposition: Model products, brands, ranges and distribution relationships independently from the page layout.
Keep the storefront modular so commerce, content and future operational integrations can evolve separately.
Use the public shop as a clear consumer surface over a structured product system.

role.summary: Commerce architecture, product and brand modelling, storefront engineering, interface design, independent deployment and operational planning.

architecture.title: Product catalogue
architecture.description: Provides structured product records, ranges, variants and consumer-facing presentation.

architecture.title: Brand and exclusivity model
architecture.description: Allows products and ranges to retain their identity and relationship to Community Supplies.

architecture.title: Storefront experience
architecture.description: Translates the underlying catalogue into a responsive, navigable retail interface.

architecture.title: Operational boundary
architecture.description: Leaves fulfilment, distribution and later integrations able to change without rewriting the product presentation.

currentState.summary: The live project establishes the independent public storefront, product presentation and modular commerce direction.

plannedDevelopment.summary: The next operational phases deepen catalogue management, fulfilment relationships and distribution workflows.

significance: Community Supplies shows commerce engineering as product, catalogue and operational architecture—not merely the visual assembly of an online shop.

eyebrow: LIVING ARCHIVE AND PERSONAL SAVING PLATFORM
definition: A public and personal archive platform connecting authored SaveSites, media objects and user-owned collections through a deliberate language of saving.
context: SaveOurs revisits a long-held identity and develops it into a system for preserving, organising and carrying meaningful material.
The public archive, authored collection pages and private My Saves cabinet form different views of the same saving model.
challenge: A saved item must retain enough source, context and collection meaning to remain useful after it leaves its original page.
Public discovery, authored collections and private ownership need distinct permissions and journeys without becoming disconnected products.
proposition: Represent saved material as structured objects connected to source, collection and user state.
Separate public SaveSites from the signed-in personal cabinet while preserving a clear route between them.
Use the SOS and barcode-coded identity as a meaningful system rather than decoration.

role.summary: Product architecture, archive and object modelling, public and signed-in interface engineering, identity-language development and human-system translation.

architecture.title: Public archive
architecture.description: Provides discovery and access to saved media, ideas and authored collections.

architecture.title: SaveSites
architecture.description: Creates contextual, authored collection views rather than undifferentiated bookmark folders.

architecture.title: My Saves
architecture.description: Gives each signed-in user a private cabinet for material deliberately carried from the wider archive.

architecture.title: Identity language
architecture.description: Encodes SOS, SaveOurS and barcode rhythm into a recognisable system tied to preservation and retrieval.

currentState.summary: The project has a developed public website, SaveSite and My Saves interface direction, plus a documented multi-generation identity system.

plannedDevelopment.summary: Further implementation will deepen object provenance, saving actions, account state and archive relationships.

significance: SaveOurs demonstrates how identity, archive modelling and personal software can combine around a clear human action: deciding what should be carried forward.

heroImage.caption: The public entry point to the SaveOurs living archive

definition: A connected product and identity system translating the MiCKz brand into recognisable products, digital assets and a public web experience.
context: MiCKz contains distinct identity, product and digital-output work that should be understood as one connected system rather than isolated artwork.
challenge: The project needs enough structure to connect brand language, product development and digital presentation without treating every asset as an independent project.
proposition: Use the project record as the parent system and retain identity, products and digital assets as separate evidence-backed contributions.

currentState.summary: MiCKz has documented identity, product-system and digital-asset contributions connected to one project record.

plannedDevelopment.summary: The case study can expand as further product and implementation evidence is made public.

significance: MiCKz shows how a recognisable brand is carried through product, identity and digital presentation rather than ending at a logo.

heroImage.alt: MiCKz website and product identity system
heroImage.caption: MiCKz public digital experience

definition: A mature speculative, philosophical and cognitive storytelling universe spanning different levels of accessibility, formats and audiences, with children's stories retained as one clearly bounded section.
context: Thinquanauts is being reimagined around a broader writing background and mixed-age audience rather than organised primarily as a children's-story website.
Its stories explore cognition, identity, perception, systems and world-models through different narrative forms.
challenge: The public structure must hold mature speculative work, accessible stories and children's publishing without making one audience define the entire project.
Related ProtoSynthesis publication families need clear relationships without collapsing distinct fictional and non-fictional outputs together.
proposition: Present Thinquanauts as the parent story and publishing world.
Organise works by audience, accessibility, format and thematic route rather than by a single age category.
Keep children's stories visible but intentionally isolated as one section of a wider universe.

role.summary: Publishing-system architecture, story-world definition, information architecture, editorial framing, website engineering and identity direction.

architecture.title: Story universe
architecture.description: Holds the shared speculative and cognitive territory across stories, worlds and recurring ideas.

architecture.title: Audience routes
architecture.description: Allows mature, general, accessible and children's work to be discovered without flattening them into one category.

architecture.title: Publication families
architecture.description: Connects books, stories, serial work and related ProtoSynthesis expressions while retaining their own identities.

architecture.title: Public reading surface
architecture.description: Provides a website structure capable of presenting the wider writing practice and later publication releases.

currentState.summary: The repository and foundational canon structure exist, and the public framing is being rebuilt around the larger mixed-age publishing world.

plannedDevelopment.summary: The next phase establishes the complete public information architecture and begins connecting publication records, story routes and evidence.

significance: Thinquanauts demonstrates publishing architecture as a system for preserving creative breadth rather than forcing an entire body of writing into its most immediately accessible category.

evidence.note: Public imagery will be connected when the newly organised project assets are available in the repository.
